clauses.reason: Terminated by its own terms at the close of Friday, December 26, 1958, the only day the order names, on which it excuses covered employees from duty all day. The leave-policy paragraph refers to the holiday period without dates, so it adds no later stated day; it is read as tied to the excused day. Recorded as 1958-12-26, inclusive. Alternatives disclosed: the exclusive reading (the end when December 26 begins) and a broader reading under which the leave direction would extend through the unspecified holiday period. Actor: the order itself. The dossier holds no own-terms record, so the end cites the order's own clause, which contains the stated day. No later amending event is held.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10792 (23 FR 9307, PDF pages 1-1; Federal Register issue of December 3, 1958; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10792.txt), headed Executive Order 10792, signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower on November 28, 1958. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Excusing Federal Employees From Duty All Day on December 26, 1958). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers all three paragraphs. The first excuses covered employees from duty all day on Friday, December 26, 1958, the day after Christmas, and treats that day as a holiday for the purposes of Executive Order 10358 of June 9, 1952 and of the statutes on compensation and leave, with exceptions for employees excluded by agency heads or whose absence would be inconsistent with law. The second directs agency heads, to the extent consistent with the needs of the service, to adopt a liberal policy for annual leave for employees who wish to take leave over the holiday period; it states no dates. The third says the order does not excuse employees whose posts of duty are required for national security or other public reasons. Own terms: the only stated day is December 26, 1958. The leave direction speaks of the holiday period without defining it, so no held text fixes a later end for it; I treat it as tied to the excused day and record the end at the close of December 26, 1958, inclusive, and disclose two alternatives: the exclusive reading (end when that day begins) and a broader reading under which the leave direction would run to the end of the Christmas and New Year period, which the order does not date. The three chosen machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes plus operative sentences of 17521 saved order texts) each state their coverage with no warning; their coverage notes were read. They search by this order's number, and none returned a hit for it.

savings.reason: The order contains no savings, exception or transitional clause; I read the whole text. Pay and leave for the excused day rest on the compensation and leave statutes, for which the order treats the day as a holiday; those effects are completed and do not keep the order operative after December 26, 1958.
